name: Aqua Green
lede: Aqua green is a modern color name; Paterson defines it as a light bluish green, built on the web color aqua.

sections.title: What the name means
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines *aquagreen* as a light bluish green [1]. The base word is *aqua*, a light greenish blue that web page creators adopted as a color name, and which Paterson ties to the X11 color set [1]. Aquamarine, the pale bluish green of sea water, is a close neighbor in the same book [1].

The books say little more. The strongest trace is a modern one: a cotton breeder looking at a boll from a plant bred from two brown parents found raw cotton of an entirely unexpected color, a kind of aqua green, described as sea turquoise mixed with moss and mint [2]. Beyond that, no history of the name turns up in our books.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Aqua green is not a painter's color. No painting in our archive of 23,781 has a color within a small distance of this swatch covering even 1% of the canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole [3].

notes.cite: ColorHub archive, 23,781 museum paintings as photographed (data/graph/fieldnotes, CIEDE2000)

questions.q: Paterson defines aquagreen as a light version of which color?
True or false: this color covers at least 1% of any painting in our archive.

openers: Aqua started as a web-page color name before it was ever a paint.

issues: Lede said vivid sea-colored green; Paterson says light bluish green, lede reworded
